transcript:
[00:00:00] Sam Carter: hey everybody, thanks for joining. this is Sam from Redwood, AE on the account. we also have Priya from the SE team. how's everyone doing?
[00:00:08] Alex Moreno: good, thanks. busy but good. appreciate you fitting us in.
[00:00:12] Maya Chen: afternoon. quick note, we have folks in london and singapore on the call today.
[00:00:18] Priya Nayar: awesome, thanks. quick agenda — we want to understand your networking constraints and residency needs, map out how Redwood Private or Dedicated would sit in your VPC, and identify any blockers for a pilot. sound good?
[00:00:30] Omar Ruiz: yes, main thing for us is country-level restrictions. we operate in UK, some EU countries, and APAC but we cannot egress to certain jurisdictions. also we need to ensure keys never leave our control.
[00:00:00] Sam Carter: got it. can you walk us through your current infra — are you on a single cloud? do you use transit/centralized egress?
[00:00:46] Jared Kim: we're primarily on BigCloud (us-east and eu-west regions). we route most outbound through a centralized transit gateway in our primary account and use interface endpoints for internal services. we do have per-region NATs for egress filtering.
[00:01:05] Priya Nayar: okay so transit gateway with centralized egress, interface endpoints — that maps well to a Redwood Private deployment. we typically offer two patterns: one is VPC peering from your VPC to our private VPCs with PrivateLink-like interface endpoints, the other is a transit-gateway attach where we attach as a spoke and keep routing centralized. each has tradeoffs — peering is simpler but can become hard to manage at scale, transit gateway gives central control and deterministic egress.
[00:01:35] Alex Moreno: question on peering — does that force us to open broad routes? security team worries about routing tables getting messy.
[00:01:42] Priya Nayar: good call out. with cross-account peering you end up managing route entries per peering, whereas transit allows prefix-based propagation and you can keep tighter controls. for Lakemont I'd expect transit fit given your centralized egress. the Redwood Private control plane can sit in a dedicated management VPC if you want.
[00:02:05] Maya Chen: and what about private endpoints? can we use interface endpoints from our subnets to hit Redwood without hairpinning through internet?
[00:02:12] Sam Carter: yes, we support interface-style private endpoints. in AWS that's PrivateLink/ENIs, in GCP it maps to private service connect. we sometimes call them private endpoints in the docs. note — some customers prefer VPC peering for lower latency but PrivateLink is more controlled for security since you only get the service IPs.
[00:02:34] Omar Ruiz: latency is a factor for us but compliance and auditability are higher priority. can we ensure flow logs and audit logs are shipped to our S3/Cloud Storage for retention?
[00:02:45] Priya Nayar: absolutely — we can deliver audit logs, request traces, and per-token billing metadata to your accounts. we typically push logs via cross-account role to a customer logging bucket; retention policies and encryption with your KMS are supported.
[00:03:02] Alex Moreno: about keys — we want HSM-backed keys and to bring our own key material where possible. is that supported?
[00:03:08] Sam Carter: yes, BYOK with HSM is supported for Redwood Private and Dedicated. you can attach your KMS (we integrate with cloud KMSs and some HSM providers). for hosted we have managed keys only, but for Private deployments you retain key control.
[00:03:24] Leah Park: timeline — we want a POC by end of Q3 to validate egress and latency. is that achievable?
[00:03:30] Priya Nayar: likely yes. typical POC is 2–4 weeks to validate connectivity, a small model, and egress behavior. we'll need your network team to open a few things and respond to testing.
[00:03:41] Jared Kim: what exact ports and IPs do you need?
[00:03:45] Priya Nayar: for transit attach we need BGP peering and a shared prefix range; we can provide ranges for private endpoints. generally no broad internet egress is required for the data plane once PrivateLink is in place, but some control-plane calls may hit Redwood control plane depending on mode. we'll send a network checklist.
[00:04:05] Alex Moreno: country constraints — we have contractual restrictions that model inference for certain customers must not route through or store data in specified countries. can Redwood guarantee region residency?
[00:04:16] Sam Carter: yes — with Redwood Private we can deploy control plane and compute in selected regions only. for Hosted/Shared customers we can't make country-level guarantees. for Dedicated and Private you can pin regions, and we can do EU-only or UK-only deployments. there's some lead time for provisioning.
[00:04:36] Omar Ruiz: lead time — how long to stand up EU-only?
[00:04:39] Priya Nayar: ballpark, 2–6 weeks depending on capacity and model footprint. if you need specific hardware (like A100 or latest) it can be longer. for quick POC we do smaller instance types.
[00:04:51] Maya Chen: we also need to understand egress IPs — our customers have allowlists. can you provide stable egress IPs per-region?
[00:04:59] Sam Carter: yes, per-deployment egress IP pools are provided for Dedicated and Private. we can also terminate egress through your NATs using transit so the egress will be your IPs.
[00:05:12] Jared Kim: okay makes sense. Priya, you mentioned control-plane calls. do they traverse public internet? we prefer all control-plane traffic over private connectivity.
[00:05:21] Priya Nayar: for Redwood Private we can optionally route control-plane traffic over your VPC peering or private link. Hosted obviously uses public endpoints. again depends on deployment mode — Private gives you choice.
[00:05:34] Alex Moreno: curious about model updates and KV cache — how are model artifacts pulled into our VPC? any outbound from our side?
[00:05:41] Priya Nayar: model artifacts are pulled into the compute nodes in the deployment; for Private you host compute in your cloud and our runtime pulls layers from our artifact registry. we can stage artifacts in your account or allow pull from our S3 with signed URLs. if you want zero external egress we can stage within your account.
[00:05:58] Omar Ruiz: notes — need ACLs for artifact storage, and sign-off from compliance on staging approach.
[00:06:04] Sam Carter: noted. question — what parts of the org own compliance sign-off?
[00:06:09] Omar Ruiz: security + legal; I'll be the tech owner and I will loop in legal once we have a template.
[00:06:15] Leah Park: can you also show cost delta between Dedicated reserved vs Private on our infra? we're trying to evaluate run-cost vs control.
[00:06:23] Sam Carter: yes we can provide a cost model. generally Dedicated is Redwood-managed capacity with predictable throughput and SLA; Private is you run compute in your account so your infra cost + Redwood platform fee. we'll share a sample TCO worksheet.
[00:06:38] Maya Chen: any differences in latency or throughput between Private and Dedicated?
[00:06:42] Priya Nayar: Dedicated has the advantage of our tuned runtime on colocated GPUs — lower variance in latency for steady throughput. Private can be equally performant if you choose similar hardware but you also take on infra ops. sometimes Private has slightly higher cold-start latency if the KV cache isn't warmed in your environment — we offer cache prewarming for POCs.
[00:07:05] Alex Moreno: ok good. a few nitty-gritty: do you support SAML SSO via Okta for the console? and RBAC?
[00:07:12] Sam Carter: yes, SAML/SSO with Okta is supported across Hosted/Dedicated/Private; RBAC is configurable and audit logs include user actions.
[00:07:21] Omar Ruiz: regulatory — do you have SOC 2 Type II and ISO attestations available?
[00:07:25] Sam Carter: yes, we'll share our SOC 2 report and ISO certificates; for Private we also provide architectural notes and can run security reviews.
[00:07:33] Leah Park: competitor question — we looked at ModelServeCo. they offered an appliance we could run on-prem but their integration with our transit gateway looked rough.
[00:07:42] Priya Nayar: yeah we see that a lot. unlike an appliance, Redwood Private focuses on running in your cloud accounts with the control plane optional — so less to manage on-prem.
[00:07:52] Alex Moreno: one more — our legal asked whether logs and tokens used for billing could be anonymized before leaving the country.
[00:07:58] Sam Carter: we can scrub PII and only export aggregate billing metrics; for Private the billing metadata can stay in your account. we'll need to review exact fields to confirm.
[00:08:12] Maya Chen: thanks. for network specifics, what's required from our side for BGP with transit?
[00:08:19] Priya Nayar: we'll need an ASN and a prefix pool to advertise. we can do BGP over VPN for initial POC. we'll share a network worksheet with port lists and example route tables.
[00:08:33] Jared Kim: do you support cross-region replication for KV cache? for latency we might want regional warm caches.
[00:08:40] Priya Nayar: yes, we support regional KV cache strategies — either local caches per-region or a warm sync. there are trade-offs in cost vs consistency; for low-latency inference we recommend local cache per-region.
[00:08:56] Alex Moreno: what about country blackout? meaning, if we need to ensure requests from a certain customer never hit compute in X country, can we enforce that?
[00:09:04] Sam Carter: yes, by restricting which regions are in the deployment and routing requests through region-aware routers. for Hosted you'd be limited, but for Private/Dedicated you can set region allowlists and Redwood's routing will honor them.
[00:09:18] Omar Ruiz: let's talk about testing — for the POC how do we validate egress and residency?
[00:09:24] Priya Nayar: we typically run synthetic traffic that includes geo-tagged payloads and verify via traceroutes, flow logs, and application-level telemetry. we'll include checks for public IPs and country routing.
[00:09:36] Leah Park: ok, that works. fun question: will Redwood help with runbook for incident response around model regressions?
[00:09:44] Sam Carter: yes, Redwood Optimize and Console include quality monitoring and you can set regression alerts tied to prompt sets. we can include runbooks in the POC deliverables.
[00:09:56] Jared Kim: one operational detail — do we need to open any inbound ports on our firewall for the attached Redwood spokes?
[00:10:02] Priya Nayar: generally no inbound from the public internet; for transit attachments the routing handles it. for PrivateLink you'll open a connection endpoint and have ENI-based IPs. we'll clarify exact security group rules in the checklist.
[00:10:16] Alex Moreno: if we move forward, who will be the single point of contact from Redwood for the infra side?
[00:10:20] Sam Carter: Priya will own the technical onboarding. I'll stay as AE. Priya: confirm?
[00:10:25] Priya Nayar: yep, I'll be the SE lead and manage the deep-dive.
[00:10:29] Omar Ruiz: noted. I'll coordinate legal and provide the restricted country list.
[00:10:33] Sam Carter: great. we should also talk about network testing windows — we may need to schedule a brief maintenance window to validate BGP and NAT flows.
[00:10:42] Maya Chen: fine. minor — do you have any docs on performance tuning for inference throughput when using our NATs and transit? we've seen TCP-multiplexing issues before.
[00:10:52] Priya Nayar: yes, we have tuning docs — kernel TCP settings, socket reuse, backoff tuning; we'll attach those with the checklist.
[00:11:04] Alex Moreno: thanks everyone — let's recap and confirm next steps.
[00:11:08] Sam Carter: recap: Redwood to share Private deployment checklist, network worksheet, SOC 2 and compliance artifacts, and a preliminary pricing/TCO. Priya to set up transit-gateway technical deep-dive. Lakemont to send restricted countries list and egress allowlist. POC target: validate egress and latency by end of Q3.
[00:11:28] Leah Park: sounds good.
[00:11:30] Omar Ruiz: quick clarifying comment — for the KMS integration we need to know supported cloud KMS providers and whether we can rotate keys without downtime.
[00:11:39] Priya Nayar: supported KMS: BigCloud KMS, EU-KMS, and HSM providers via standard APIs. rotation without downtime is supported if you follow the KMS rotation pattern we provide; we'll include the doc.
[00:11:52] Jared Kim: any blockers from Redwood side to start the POC next week?
[00:11:56] Sam Carter: no blockers; depends on your network team availability. we'll send the checklist today and aim to schedule the deep-dive in the next few days.
[00:12:05] Alex Moreno: perfect. thanks all. we'll follow up in email.
[00:12:10] Sam Carter: thanks everyone — talk soon.
